_comment: The branch protection rule enforced on `main`, recorded so a clone can see it.
GitHub holds the authoritative copy server-side and NOTHING syncs this file:
editing it changes no rule, and changing the rule in the UI does not update it.
It exists so the protection is auditable from the repository and so a change to
it is reviewed rather than clicked. Apply with:
`contexts: [ci]` must match the job id in workflows/ci.yml, which deliberately
has no `name:` — GitHub names a check run after the job's `name:` when one is
set. A required check that never reports does not disable the rule; it pins
every PR at Expected and blocks the merge.
`enforce_admins: true` is the point of the exercise. Without it the repo owner
keeps an implicit bypass, the merge button stays green on a failing PR, and the
rule protects nobody who could actually break `main`.
`required_approving_review_count: 0` because this is a single-author repository.
Requiring an approval would lock the only author out of their own main branch;
the PR itself is the gate here, and the status check is what has teeth.
GitHub ignores unknown keys, so this comment is inert on PUT.
